utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And could you remind you sir that the affirmation that you made is still applicable. I understand that you may have a correction you wish to make to something you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. [Interpretation] Your Honours, I did review -- or I have in mind my statement that I need to speak the truth and nothing but the truth, and this intervention I'm making precisely with regards to that. Yesterday, in the answer to one of the questions asked by the Defence of Mr. Apostolski, when speaking about the dismissal of Mr. Gzim Ostreni discharged from the Kosovo Protection Corps and the post of head of the General Staff, I was interrupted by the learned Prosecutor, and he openly doubted that I was speaking the truth. I made efforts yesterday and during the night to analyse my statement and to find a verification for that. And for my sake and for the sake of truth, I wish to indicate to the Honourable Court that corroboration for that statement can be found in the statement 65 ter 2D712. It is in the footnote when clarifying my paragraphs from the report, numbers 265 and 266. I wish to indicate that what we have here is a document, a research, prepared for presentation at the annual convention of the America Association of Political Scientists in 2001 in San Francisco, California. The title is: Calm before the storm, the impact of the cross-border networks, corruption, and smuggling on to the stability of Macedonia and the security in the region, prepared by professor, Dr. Robert Hislow, Ph.D. in political science within the Union College in New York. On page 34 and 35 in that paragraph in the second sentence, and I quote it says: "In April, Gzim Ostreni, veteran of the NLA -- or KLA from Debar, Macedonia, was suspended from his office in the Kosovo Protection Corps because of the cooperation with the NLA." I made efforts, Your Honours, to arrive at a more precise answer with regard to this position of the esteemed Professor Hislow; and in my electronic archives which I have brought here to The Hague, I found yet another corroboration for this position and this statement that I have made, in the information coming from the state, Macedonia Information Agency, dated the 13th of April, 2001. The title is: The head of the Kosovo Protection Corps dismissed, discharged. It is three sentences only and I will read it: Pristina, 13th of April, MIA, the commander of the Kosovo Protection Corps, Agim Ceku, today discharged the chief of this formation, Gzim Ostreni, because of the suspicions that he participated in the attacks of the Albanian terrorists in Macedonia as related by MIA. "The spokespersons of the corps, Muharem Mahmutaj, announced that Ostreni will be demobilised if the suspicions of his involvement in the events in Macedonia are proven. Mahmutaj stressed that the primary objective of the corps is protection of its own institutions and not certain members of it." Author of this information is the MIA journalist, with the initials are "TT." The information was made available to the public by the person with the initials "SB" at 1704 on the 13th of April, 2001. So, in conclusion, I believe that what I stated with regards to the discharge of Mr. Gzim Ostreni from the post -- from his office in the Kosovo Protection Corps is correct, with a slight correction. I believe that I stated 14th of April, while it was actually the 13th of April, and this is why the esteemed Prosecutor, in my opinion, had no right nor duty to interrupt me when I was presenting my position. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could I point out to that the Prosecutor's conduct is under our control, and there would, in our view, be nothing critical that could be said about his appropriate concern expressed yesterday. But we are grateful for your additional references, which I'm sure will be taken into account by counsel as they question you. Now, Mr. Apostolski. Ms. Residovic. We've moved.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Dr. Markovski. I would kindly, as you, Dr. Markovski, to you look again at this exhibit, 1D81. It is after tab 3. That is page 1D3042, Macedonian, and it was 1D3048 in the English version. Do you remember, Dr. Markovski, that yesterday, near the end of the day, we discussed the issuance of President Trajkovski's decision to establish a defence of the city and some elements of the command issued by the commander of the city defence, General Sokol Mitrevski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the last thing we discussed was the neighbouring zones of responsibility to the one of General Sokol Mitrevski, actually, to the one of command of the city defence. Do you remember that that was the last thing we discussed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, considering your answers with regards to what neighbours denotes, was it proper to say that neighbours to the units that were under the command of Commander Sokol Mitrevski were the units in the neighbouring cities, Tetovo and Kumanovo?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say so, unless the task relates to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it could also be said that all the other units participating in the defence of the city, as you said, it was not only the army and the police but also civilian defence. They all had the duties to follow the commands of the commander of the city defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we have this page. And if in item 3, the notion of neighbours has under number 1, command post of the forces, described in item 1, is in the barracks KJP2 in Tetovo, it is means that they are neighbours to the command of the city defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is why I told you if the units you have mentioned which are under the command of General Mitrevski are not involved in this action, then they are neighbours. But at the same time, considering the zone of responsibility of the neighbouring unit, in this case, this is the command of the Kuzman Jasifovski Pitu barracks in Tetovo. So, yes, it is exactly as you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In item 2, we have other forces indicated. The command post of which is in HT Karpos in Kumanovo. Those would be other neighbours to the zone under the command of Sokol Mitrevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So in this case, the western neighbour, the unit -- to the unit that was given the task was the barracks Kuzman Jasifovski Pitu in Tetovo, while the eastern zone with its own responsibility is the command in the barracks Hristijan Todorovski Karpos in Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Petrovac airport is within the zone of command of the city defence. Is one of the main reasons? So the defence of the airport was one of the reasons to establish the city defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So further in this item entitled "Neighbours," it is says: "The forces of anti-aircraft defence..." and I don't know what "VV" stands for.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It stands for aviation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "... are based at the airport Petrovac from where they conduct air force support to the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia in the fight against the terrorists acting upon call." Could you agree with me that this is an order pertaining to the units under a command, and not the neighbours?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, precisely. Specifically, it pertains to the units involved and who have tasks within this zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We saw previously that amongst the reason of the establishment For the city defence and its command was the village of Aracinovo. Do you agree, Dr. Markovski, that the village of Aracinovo was under the command of General Sokol Mitrevski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This area was under the command and under the control of the units that General Mitrevski had under his command. It was under his zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The next paragraph from the top of this page reads: "The forces of the MOI, Ministry of Interior, blocked the village of Aracinovo and controlled the access points to the village. With appropriate forces they secure the facilities of vital importance in the central city area." Do you agree with me, Dr. Markovski, that we have here the Ministry of Interior, not as a neighbour, but as a force under the command of General Sokol Mitrevski?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are within the forces under the command of General Mitrevski.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is a direct order that the forces of the Ministry of Interior have the duty to follow. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: An order that is operationalised with precisely provided tasks for the forces of the MOI.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look at the document in tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit 1D82.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document bearing the date 14th of June, and it is again signed by Sokol Mitrevski and that is a marching order. And in item 5.1.1, the task pertains to the 1st Guardist Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With regards to this, I wish to draw your attention to item 1, which reads: "Data on the terrorists, information about the terrorists," and it says, "according to the defence orders." Do you agree with me, Dr. Markovski, if I were to say that this, 1st Guardist Brigade, and it can be seen from the order that it was deployed in the area of Ilinden barracks and the village of Ljubanci, that it had the same tasks with regards to the terrorists as those given in the order for the defence of the city of Skopje that we had seen before.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although we have here two documents, they pertain to one and the same task, to execute the task given to the 1st Guardist Brigade, the commander for the defence of the city of Skopje has decided to issue a marching order as well, so they would occupy their positions and be able to respond to the obligations entailed in the task. So my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the task of the 1st Guardist Brigade was as well, to destroy or to detect and destroy the sabotage terrorist groups and to prevent their entry in the city of Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Once the president or the commander of the city defence has issued the basic order for the defence, do you agree with me, Dr. Markovski, that then the military superior, regardless of the rank up to the Supreme Commander, was able to directly issue orders to the individual units of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if the task involves them and if they fall under the zone Of responsibility where they perform tasks jointly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly did you now to look at the document in tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit 1D314. Page is 1D4809, and the English page is 1D8176.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document from the General Staff of the army of Republic of Macedonia, command of the security forces. And before I ask the question related to this document, tell me, does the title, command of the security forces, indicate clearly that the security forces comprised both army and the police?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So what we have here is a document from the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, command of the security forces, date is 21st of June, 2001. Do you agree with me that this is after the new Law on Defence has been passed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 21st of June is after the adoption of the new Law on Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this document is addressed to ESZ, a unit for special tasks of the Ministry of Interior. Are you aware that the unit for special tasks is the unit Tiger, the only special unit in the Ministry of Interior at that time? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Beneath this, it says that this is a combat order. Tell me whether this document, so the General Staff directly issuing a combat order to a unit of the Ministry of Interior, agrees with your military knowledge but also with the actual situation as existed in 2001?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's be more precise in this case. It is not the General Staff issuing direct order to the unit for special tasks that belongs to the MOI. It is the commander of the command for security forces which is under the direct command of the General Staff of the army of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. We did not see who was issuing this order, but it corroborates your position. If the units were placed in a situation that they work jointly with the army under the same command, then it is the army's superiors who can issue a direct order to the units of police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is obvious from this order. So, yes, it is correct. It is precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Regardless of the amending of the law, and you clearly stated that the old law with regards to the competencies of the president and the way the army did not really change, could you confirm, Dr. Markovski, that neither pursuant to the old law, nor pursuant to the new law, and not even today, it is the minister of the interior who can order deployment of police forces for any combat activity?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correctly. The minister of the interior does not have that right under any law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Answering the questions of my learned colleague, Apostolski, you stated that the sabotage terrorist groups had uniforms at times, but there were situations also where they were active wearing civilian clothes and they often used the civilian population to withdraw there after their actions. Do you remember testify to go this effect?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I remember having stated this, and I based this not only on my personal knowledge but also on documents developed by the international factor that was present in the Republic of Macedonia during the crisis.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The order by the commander of the city defence, that we analysed a moment ago, includes also the order to prevent the disguised sabotage terrorist groups from entering the city. Do you remember -- do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is one of the tasks and obligations of the structures of security forces involved in this task and action.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Ljuboten case that you analysed in detail in your report, after the end of combat activities in the village itself, one part of the population withdrew towards Skopje. You are familiar with this, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I noted this in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering your previous experience, as you stated, but also the positions you took into account and which were prepared by the international community, at the list, there was a real threat that part of the sabotage terrorist groups that were inside the village would, as was the usual practice of the NLA, enter the city, together with the civilian population. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a real threat, and it was already confirmed that this is what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That really threat, or risk, as you stated, and as you stated it, did actually happen, was based on the fact that just a few days before these events, an armed group was detected and eliminated it Skopje. It had infiltrated there in order to execute terrorist activities inside the city. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In one of the settlements of the city of Skopje is where it took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was the terrorist group Teli. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was led by Teli.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter kindly asks the counsel and witness to pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you agree with me, Dr. Markovski, if I say that the order for the defence of the city of Skopje, in this specific case as well, when the action to detect the terrorists in the village of Ljuboten was concerned, presupposes also preventing sabotage terrorist groups from penetrating the city of Skopje?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you would neglect this, then the task would not be really executed, and it would not really make sense, the action itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So an order issued to the forces to capture the terrorists presupposes at least the necessary checking up of persons who entered the city of Skopje through the check-points. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I may conclude, that then the activity of the security forces at the check-points, in order to prevent their entry into the city of Skopje would be part of the combat activities taking place in the Skopje and comprised by the same order that actually ordered the action. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be a constituent part of the course of the action.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Just for the purpose of the transcript, I would like to say that the Exhibit 1D93 has been uploaded in the e-court under the number "2D731" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Instead of "1D93," it should read "2D93."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what was that exhibit, could you remind me, please, Mr. Apostolski?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received now as an exhibit in the Trial.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit number 2D00093. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you're ready, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We do have several binders of exhibits that I hope to discuss with the witness, and perhaps we could provide the first binder right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Over the next hour or so, is that it, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's the hope, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Markovski, my name it is Dan Saxon, and I represent the Prosecutor in these proceedings. I'm originally from Boston, Massachusetts in the United States, and I have a number of questions that I'd like to ask you. First of all, yesterday, at page 10614 of the transcript, in response to a question from my colleague, you said that you disagreed that the events of 2001 in the Republic of Macedonia should be defined as classic war or classic armed conflict. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Doctor, in a -- in a classic armed conflict, one of the things that happens often is that soldiers are mobilised and deployed to areas where fighting is occurring. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just in the classical type of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. But I'm going to ask you some questions right now just focussing on the concept that you mentioned yesterday of the classic armed conflict. All right. But in response to my last question, effectively, your answer would be a yes, right, that in a classic armed conflict, soldiers are mobilised and deployed to areas of fighting? Correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the classic armed conflict, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in a classic armed conflict, both sides use a variety of weapons against the other side. Correct? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we have to define when discussing the classic armed conflict. This would mean the use of enemy activities and weaponry between two state entities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Between two state entities. Well, are you familiar with the concept of internal armed conflict? Are you familiar with that concept?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with the concept of an internal armed Conflict, which is very difficult to be defined, because - and I was discussing this yesterday - it is a transitional stage between the crisis and armed conflict. An internal armed conflict may be caused also by internal structures, and I do agree with that. Maybe one should add that the basic characteristic of any armed conflict, thus internal conflicts as well, are the fights and combat activities that are taking place in a planned manner and in a certain continue unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. But just so that I understand your last answer, you say that an internal armed conflict is the transitional stage between a crisis and an armed conflict. Did I hear you correctly?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crisis has its own development stage, basically three stages of development --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, I understand that. You explained that very well yesterday. I completely understand the three stages of the crisis, as you explained them yesterday. But I'm just trying to clarify your last question, Doctor. You said that an internal armed conflict is a transitional stage between the Crisis and armed conflict, and I'm just trying to understand that -- that point. Is an internal armed conflict, therefore, an armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the condition that it has a character of fighting and combat activities that they should be taking place planned and in continuity. This means that there should be organised military structures that issue orders and operations that are being conducted according to previously prepared orders and commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Going back, I'll use the term you used a minute ago, basic characteristics of an armed conflict, if you will. A basic characteristic of an armed conflict is that both sides use a variety of weapons against the other side, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are leading me to something again that is something I cannot accept as completely true, because in order for an armed conflict to exist, internal one as well, one should see a couple of sides. This means that both sides, if they are armed forces, they have to be organised according to the standards for organisation and functioning of armed forces. They should have a planned conduction of military activities and combat activities, and they should be taking place in continuity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry. Perhaps my question wasn't clear. Let me put the question slightly differently. Let's suppose, hypothetically, that an armed conflict exists in country X, all right? One common characteristic of an armed conflict is that the two sides use a variety of weapons against each other, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not so, because weapons can be used also by terrorists. Weapons might be used by armed extremists, regardless of whether we are talking about terrorists originating from the country or global Terrorism. That is why I was telling that one of the basic characteristics, in order for a process to be characterised where violent means are being used, you have to have sides; that is to say, it should be done by two armed organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you have those two armed organisations fighting in an armed conflict, oftentimes, they use a variety of different weapons against each other, correct, when those conditions exist?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. When these conditions are met, they would use the weaponry that they dispose of.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you have two organised armed organisations fighting in an armed conflict, then it's also common that soldiers get killed and wounded, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we still talking about the country X?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And still talking about country X, the armed conflict in country X, classic armed conflict, it is also common that civilians would be displaced, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is, unfortunately, an accompanying consequence when you have military actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it would also be common then, wouldn't it, in such an armed conflict, that one side takes control of some territory that previously belonged to the other side, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, the goal of the armed conflicts is precisely this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And it would also be common that both opposing sides, both armed groups, would fortify their positions with items like sandbags, trenches, things like that? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If they conduct active combat activities, then they would be involved in this type of activities; that is to say, in order to protect their own forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And in such a classic armed conflict, in country X, at least there so-called modern wars or modern armed conflicts, it is also common that international actors become involved, such as the ICRC, such as the United Nations, such as NATO. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly. Because the modern wars, in this sense, as you would present them, they do not have these types of characteristics. This is the characteristics of the classical wars in the past. The typical activity of the modern war would be the asymmetrical activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you refer to asymmetrical activities in modern war, are you referring to guerilla warfare, insurgency?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just guerilla warfare. The most typically threat in the present time, regarding security, is the terrorism, especially global terrorism. The guerilla warfare is not a characteristic of the modern democratic states.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But it is possible that, in a modern democratic state, a guerilla or insurgent army can development, can't it? Hasn't that happened in modern history?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why guerilla warfare would develop in modern democracies if the problems that which occur, and which a normal social process in every country with a difference intensity, could be resolved with normal democratic and political means.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But if problems which occur are not resolved with normal democratic and political means, an insurgency can develop, can't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Insurgency is also a characteristic in the past. I fully disagree that the uprising or the insurgency is a characteristic of the modern democracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. In a classic armed conflict, again going back to our country X, it's also common, isn't it, that some aspects of normal life are disrupted, such as the ability of adults to go to work, the ability of children to go to school? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: People tend to spend more time inside where they feel more protected, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, really. Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if there's an armed conflict, and if you live in country X, and there's fighting going on, combat going around either in your town or close to your town and you're a civilian, you would tend to perhaps spend more time in protected areas, wouldn't you, in shelters, in basements, places where bullets won't hit you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I'm compelled to do so, this is precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And also in a classic armed conflict in country X, it's also common, isn't it, that both opposing forces often communicate to the public about their activities and their objectives. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Bearing in mind the development of technology, this is quite normal and expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, in fact, if just focussing for a moment on you and the events in 2001 in Macedonia, in 2001, when you were the army spokesperson, you communicated to the general public about the ongoing events, the activities of the NLA, and the activities of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. In 2001, I was the spokesperson of the army, not the army, but the army of the Republic of Macedonia, to be more specific. And I would like to point out that being a spokesperson means to present the official positions of the institution that is being represented by the spokesperson; that is, where he or she is working. In other words, the spokesperson is the conveyor of the news and the positions of the institution where he or she originates from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And in that sense, as the spokesperson in 2001, your work was important so that the public would understand what the security forces were doing and why. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that was important, in order to reduce fear among the general public and to avoid panic. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, for the public to be informed about everything that is going on and that is current news regarding the security situation at the Particular moment; and, number two, one might say what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Going back to our country X, in a classic armed conflict -- in a classic armed conflict, often, unfortunately, abuses against civilians are committed by both sides. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, if we discuss a specific country, we might be even more specific in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I think I'll going to come back to this topic later. But can we agree, then, that in country X, in a classic armed conflict, you often encounter the activities that I've just mentioned to you or some combination of these activities. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm wondering, please, if we can show the witness what is P00467.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Dr. Markovski, if you take that binder that was given to you, and if you turn to tab 12. Well, you may or may not see the exhibit, but if it's not in the binder, you will see it on the screen. It's simply a map of Macedonia. We'll see it in a minute. And, Dr. Markovski, obviously, this is a map of the Republic of Macedonia. I'm wondering, please, if you can focus, if you go from the city of Skopje to the west, you see there's a road that connects the city of Skopje to Tetovo. Do you see that road or highway?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it, and I know it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm wondering if our court officer could help us for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, if you could assist us, please, and if you take up the magic pen that works on that computer screen. Just to make it easier, if you can highlight please that road. Just draw a thicker line along that road from Skopje to Tetovo, please?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that -- that road, Doctor, that road is the main communication link between the city of Skopje and the city of Tetovo. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is it an additional road. This is the highway or the first grade road. There are several axillary roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And do those axillary roads go close to the highway?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them goes in parallel with the highway, and the other ones turn to the south or to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are called main and rockade roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And if this main and the rockade roads between Skopje and Tetovo were to be cut or captured, then the northwestern corner of the state becomes virtually isolated from the rest of Macedonia. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very general assumption. If this happens, we have to consider many of the preconditions. But I would say that I agree with you if the conditions are of this kind and if a force exists capable of doing something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Because of then the strategic importance of this road and the auxiliary roads, that was one reason why the NLA deployed some of its forces in the Suva Gora mountains south of Grupcin and Mount Zeden. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And we've just lost the highlighted portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could just answer my question, first.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you to repeat the question, because also I was looking at the line that was lost in the mean time. Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Maybe we can just do this in a logical order. If you can take up the pen again and draw your line again along the road, please.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, probably, I'm going to be even more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So going back to my question, one of the reasons why the NLA deployed some of its forces in the Suva Gora mountains south of Grupcin and around Mount Zeden is because of the strategic importance of that road. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is not so. One group of armed extremists were to be seen south of the road in the locality of Bojane, and other group of this type was to the north of this road on the mountain of Zeden.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bojane, there were around 30 to 50 armed extremists, and I'm not quite sure. I don't know previously about Zeden.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you help us a bit please, then, so that this is clearer. Could you draw a circle to the north of the road, approximately where Mount Zeden is?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we please zoom in on the map. I do apologise, but with my glasses, my eyesight is not that great.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's not a problem, and I'm in the same situation, so you don't need to apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We have a problem again, because if we zoom in, we're going to loose the line that you draw. What I'm going to do is to ask the court officer to let this image go, please, and zoom in on the upper left side of this map, so that we can get closer to Tetovo. Okay. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you could take up the pen again, and because you're getting very good at this now, if you can draw the line along the road.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I had a lot of practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And now if you could please draw a circle approximately where Mount Zeden is.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could you write the number 1 next to that circle.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And could you draw a circle to the south of the road, approximately where Bojane is?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure how precise I am about the locate, but this would be location, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you draw the number 2 next to that lower Circle, please.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And, of course, for the Macedonian security forces in 2001, the danger in having NLA forces at position 1 and position 2 was that that road could be cut. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I would not agree with this conclusion, because we are not discussing forces here but only groups. As I already mentioned, there were 30 to 50 armed extremists in Bojane, and a larger number in the mountain region in the mountain of Zeden. This is not a respectable force that could be able to do this. But bearing in mind they're terrorist methodology of action, they would have been able to cut off the road. They could have caused a terrorist act on the structures of the security forces and civilian that might be moving along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I will repeat, this is not a respectable force that would create or mean a serious threat to the security in this region.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, let's talk briefly, then, about the events of the 8th of August at Karpalak. On that day, I believe ten Macedonian soldiers died when the NLA ambushed an army of the Republic of Macedonia convoy. Is that right? Just say yes or no, that way we'll get through this more quickly.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say, unfortunately, the answer is yes, and I just added the word "unfortunately."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And, for example, when that incident occurred, at least temporarily at that moment, the road effectively was cut, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The Ministry of Interior ordered for two or three hours. The road was cut upon order from the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the other roads, the auxiliary roads, were open.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness -- I'd like to show a couple of video-clips to Dr. Markovski now. And, Your Honours, in your binders, you'll find the transcripts of the videos that we show. Before we leave This image, can this exhibit be admitted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P00599. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, if we can show the witness what is 65 ter 1118.15, and the transcript of this video -- this video-clip is available at tab 11 in binder 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Dr. Markovski, what you're going to see in a minute is a video-clip from Macedonian Radio and Television, from the 27th of May, 2001, taken in the region of Vaksince. And we do not seem to be getting any sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think it just came up, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Here we are. Something is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we start at the beginning, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There we see, Dr. Markovski, what I believe to be is a combat helicopter. I wanted to ask you in what circumstances are combat helicopters used or were they used in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Excuse me, this is at 32 seconds of the clip.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So when a state is under threat, under a security threat of any nature, including also terrorist activities, pursuant to the United Nations Covenant, Article 51, the country has the right to defend itself and to undertake measures and activities --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, I'm very sorry to interrupt. I'm sorry. My question was too general. It wasn't clear enough. What I meant by my question was under what kinds of military Circumstances, what kinds of combat circumstances is a combat helicopter employed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A combat helicopter would be employed in several situation: First would be the classic combat activities. Another situation would be in a combat as a support to other security structures when dealing away with the terrorism and terrorist activities in a given territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And when you say "support to other security structures, more specifically, that would be what may be referred to as "fire support," firing rocket, firing machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Combat helicopters actually provide fire support to other structures and to the infantry primarily. Because we don't have a navy, it would be support for the infantry in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop for a moment. This is at 50 seconds of the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to tell, Dr. Markovski, whether the armoured personnel carrier that we see here behind the gentleman, are you able to whether that is a police vehicle or an army vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an armed transporter, but I really can't make a guess whether this is the army or the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But anyhow, it is in the armed transporter, APC, of the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Maybe we'll just go ahead a second or two. Well, never mind. Just keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop, please. Now we're at a minute 32.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Obviously, you can see yourself there giving a statement, Dr. Markovski. But I'd like to focus, if we can --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I would have been a lot younger than now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you're not the only one who can say that. You say, here, that the forces are not sent without a reason. Do you recall that? You said that just a minute ago in the clip?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be more precise, the forces were not sent offhand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So your assertion could be accepted as being correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if I understand things, then, the reason that the security forces were sent to the Vaksince area was because NLA units had taken control of Vaksince and other villages to the north-west of Kumanovo, and they to be driven out or killed, is that correct, or captured?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the aim of any activity of the security structures is to provide a safe environment. I would not agree with your, I would say, final position, that the aim is killings. The aim is to provide a safe environment. Unfortunately, there could be consequences of such activities, and those consequences could be killings and wounding.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue with this clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop there, please. We're now at two minutes on this video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, here, we see you again, and you say at this point: "The terrorists are trying to, in a way, redirect the focal point of the combat actions to the area of Otlja, towards Matejce." Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this pertains to the focus of the armed activities of the armed forces; that is to say, the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia. They acted in that way. They were mingling with the population leaving a region or a settlement, leaving one settlement entering another, in order to force the security structures to divert their focus on to another region.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, that may be, Doctor. But you did say here that "the terrorists are trying to, in a way, redirect the focal point of the Combat actions towards the area of Otlja towards Matejce," right, that was the official version?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's a yes?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, and I will repeat, through their activities --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's all right. If you can just confirm that that's what you said.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not what you are saying. It is what I had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. To do something like this, to redirect the focal point of combat areas, to redirect the focal point of combat to different areas, that requires a certain degree of planning, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Planning is a very complex process, and planning is preceded by an assessment of the situation, then the idea design of the activities, thinking out the activities, analysis of the situation, and only then making the decision on the activities and planning the actual activities, which means that it would be a poor commander who has not made an assessment and who would make new plans from one moment to another, as the situation unfolds in the given country X. So, in that case, he would not be able to implement the action, and he would not be able to control the activities. The only thing that he would be able to do would be planning. There is a saying: To command means to forecast.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Markovski, do we take that response as a yes or as a no?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is the one I have given you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very difficult to make a black and white picture. It would be very good if that were possible, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to give a black and white picture, but I am asking you to give a brief, clear answer to what was a brief, clear question. I'm going to ask my question again: To redirect the focal point of combat areas requires a certain degree of planning, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, planning is needed, but this is done in advance and not from one moment to another, depending on how the situation unfolds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, Doctor, that combat -- combat situations can be very fluid situations?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you be more precise, because I really don't understand what you are trying to ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fluid in our language means "empty."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then I better use another word in English. Would it be fair to say that that, during combat activities, circumstances and conditions can change very rapidly? Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And a commander has to be able to adapt to changing circumstances of combat, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He should lead the operations, the actions --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreters did not get the final part Of the answer, so if the witness could repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the last part of your response. Can you repeat it again, and just speak up a bit louder?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commander is leading the operations, the combat activities. He is not changing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, what if circumstances change during the combat activities, is the commander supposed to let his men die?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is why I told you, with regards to this, to how the situation unfolds, the commander is leading the combat activities. It is again based on the idea on how to carry out the combat activities and the advance planning of the activities where all possible scenarios could be forecasted, what would happen during the execution of the action. It would be a poor commander that changes his plan from one moment to another and who changes the combat activities. But at the end of the line, let me accept your assertion as correct, that a poor commander would change his plans. But he would be a commander for a very brief period only, trust me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, Dr. Markovski, you became an officer in the army of the Republic of Macedonia in 1973, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What year was it then?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1973, I enrolled the Military Academy in the then-Yugoslav National Army, and I returned to the Republic of Macedonia after the dissolution of Yugoslavia at the beginning of 1992, when the army was established in April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My apologies. My mistake. You became an army officer in 1973, right, when you joined the Military Academy in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So you know something about command and commanding, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We say I have a certificate confirming that I know this, because I have graduated from the command academy in Belgrade in -- actually, I graduated in 1989. I started it in 1988.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, a moment ago, you told us that it's a poor commander who would change his plans. Well, suppose an army is surrounded and needs to retreat so that it will not be destroyed. If a commander orders such a retreat, why would that commander be a poor commander?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a principle in the commanding, which pertains to what is the realistically achievable goal and through what means and forces. This is the principle of effectiveness in the command. The goal could not be achieved at any cost, at just any cost. The goal should be justified having in mind the means used and the risk, and also the forces, the soldiers used in the achieving of that goal. The commander who makes the assessment that the further achieving of the goal would be ineffective, this is why he is a commander, to then make a decision. But the decision will not be, as you say, a change in his thinking, but it would be an activity planned in advance, which has established that if the goal exceeds the cost of the means used and the casualties, this is what the commander will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, I'm going to stop you there. You haven't answered my question. My question was simple: If an army is surrounded and needs to retreat so that it will not be destroyed, if a commander changes his plan and orders a retreat, that doesn't make him a poor commander, does it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, on the contrary. If this is what the commander does within the principle of effectiveness, he would be a good commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. May I ask, may I show a bit more of this clip and ask two or three more questions before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can move forward, with my case manager's help, to what is 4 minutes and 16 seconds, please, or just before that. If we go to 4 minutes, please. Okay. Let's start from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What we've just seen is that the -- we see that the remaining commanders of the terrorist structures gathered the IDs, the identifications of the other terrorists and destroyed them. Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that it was allegedly seized, the documents. That was a comment made by the journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. And would you agree, then, that the NLA units in the Vaksince area then had commanders?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Vaksince had no units within it. There was a group more than -- less than 50 armed extremists strong who started their activities with the terrorist act against the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Markovski -- A -- vehicle of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, on the 3rd of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm just going to stop you there. My question is something different, and I'll use your term. The group, the NLA group that was in Vaksince, can we agree that they had a commander or commanders?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, but let's suppose that it was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender what is 65 ter 1118.15, the accompanying transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit number P00600. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that then a convenient time, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. JUDGE PARKER. We will adjourn now and resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please show the witness another video-clip. It is 65 ter 1118.17, and it has ERN number VOOO-7472. It will be clip 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Dr. Markovski, what you're going to see in a moment is some more video material produced by MRTV, this time on the 29th of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So if we could start that clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop there. If we could, well, keep going, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see a helicopter, which appears to be firing rockets. We see the rockets appearing to be exploding on the ground. This is around 25. Please keep going.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What we just heard, Dr. Markovski, was you explaining that the NLA had attacked with all weapons at their disposal from snipers up to mortars. I'd simply like to ask you: Doesn't the use of mortars, artillery, require a certain degree of planning and coordination during combat so that you don't shell your own soldiers? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree. It doesn't have to be planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if it's not planned, don't you run a big risk that you might kill or injure a number of your own soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with a mortar fire, because if we are talking about 120-millimetres mortars, it has a reach up to 12 kilometres. So there is no chance to injure one of your own structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, suppose some of your soldiers are operating 11 kilometres away and ask for some artillery support with mortars. Don't you need to coordinate with them so as to make sure that you don't drop shells on your own soldiers?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it is a military unit which has deployed certain units in a certain region, then this would be done. But, here, it is obvious that armed Albanian extremists are stationed, are positioned on a precisely determined location. Their structures are not located anywhere else, and that is why they can do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And where do you take that information from the video-clip that you've just seen?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From your question. I don't see this in the recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, you said, "armed Albanian extremists." You said: "Here, it is obvious that armed Albanian extremists are stationed, are positioned on a precisely determined location. Their structures are not located anywhere else, and that is why they can do this." Where are you getting that information from?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I know at that particular period where the armed extremists have been located, and they were located in the vicinity or right next to the villages where, later on, they would hide. Vaksince, Otlja, Lupate, and Slupcane are the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This particular video-clip is talking about Matejce. That's what we just saw.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In west -- to the west of Slupcane is the village of Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And how do you know for a fact that there were no NLA soldiers in the area of Matejce?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say there was or there wasn't, but the picture did not show here in which direction they fired. If you can remind me, then we can comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm just going to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we see the rest of the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, there is a gentleman here - this is at 1 minute, 7 seconds of this video - and to your left we see a gentleman wearing a blue shirt. Can you tell us who that is?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, he was the spokesperson of the ministry, and I was the spokesperson of the army. This is a close friend of mine, and today he is a leader of a political party in the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this is Mr. Gjorgji Trendafilov?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Gjorgji Trendafilov.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, when you say that Mr. Trendafilov was the spokesperson of the ministry, that's the Ministry of Defence, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Here we see that, according to this news report, the Albanian terrorists are holding persons hostage in Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This comment made by your colleague Mr. Trendafilov, he mentioned disinformation which he feels probably has the objective to discredit the dignity and honour of the army of Macedonia. Is Mr. Trendafilov referring to what is generally called propaganda?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, I have to clarify. We had several situations when foreign media most of all in their attempt to be as popular as possible, or to be able to sell their material, quite often they would use this type of information or news reports, thus showing photographs and video-clips from different countries and different regions as this was happening in the Republic of Macedonia, especially regarding the tanks 84 which did not exist in Macedonia then and also today. Exodus of civilian people that did not happen in the Republic of Macedonia, but only from Kosovo to Macedonia back in 1999. And both I and Mr. Trendafilov had to face these challenges where we would have to negate this type of reports coming from the media. In this sense, his statement was made; at least, this is my guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, he refers to a special war undertaken against the Macedonian army to discredit its dignity and its honour. I'm just -- I'm trying to clarify whether at least part of this special war involved propaganda coming from the NLA.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot be precise, but part of the special war also is propaganda; and worldwide and within Macedonia, propaganda is considered as something negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this video, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P00601. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to show you, at this time, just one more video-clip, Dr. Markovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we can show the witness what is 65 ter 1118.11. This has ERN number VOOO-7472, and it's clip 11. The transcript can be found at tab 16 of binder 1, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Dr. Markovski, this is another video-clip produced by MRTV, this time on the 18th of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop there, please. This is at 42 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And there, you mentioned, Dr. Markovski, new fortifications of the terrorists at two positions, to the north of Vaksince and also to the north-west. Do you see that? Did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This is a little forest to the north of Slupcane on the terrain between Slupcane and Vaksince.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can we continue with it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, we did not get the last part. The transcript right now is not corresponding, but we got the first part.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I just want to ask you: The construction of new fortifications by a group, wouldn't that also demonstrate a certain degree of planning and coordination?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are discussing here the activities which, upon order of the Supreme Commander, President Trajkovski, were -- was conducted by the security forces in the region of Vaksince. Pressurised by the activities of the security structures, they retreated to the region of the village of Slupcane; and during this period, when talking about new fortifications, we are basically talking about establishing the positions of mortars, positions that I mentioned earlier. We were discussing the forest to the north of Slupcane; and in the report I gave at that time in my statement, I'm talking about the part to the north-west of Slupcane, so a new fortification or a new position for the mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, if you have to decide on a new position for your artillery, doesn't that require a certain amount of planning and coordination? You don't just put your artillery anywhere, do you?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You really appreciate these extremists armed groups. There are no structures like that who would plan and who would organise, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'm just -- just so that your testimony is clear, so what you're saying is, then, that the members of the NLA would simply have placed their mortars, other artillery, wherever they felt like it. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where they considered these should be placed, not where they wanted. This would be something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Where, who considered that the mortars should be placed?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, there were experts amongst them who were taught how to operate mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And probably, then, to use your term, the experts who knew about how to operate mortars would probably also discuss with commanders where the mortars should be positioned. Isn't that right? Isn't that just logical?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Why can't you confirm it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I don't know whether they had a commander at all. If you indicate who the person is, then maybe we can discuss it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, let's suppose that we don't know whether there's a commander or not, but let's suppose there's an expert who knows about artillery. That expert in the NLA has to plan where he's going to put the mortars, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he is in a situation and possibility to plan. This was a particular, specific situation where they would leave the village of Vaksince and retreat to the village of Slupcane.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And retreat -- the term "retreat," in the military sense, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Retreat means when you're not able to fight the enemy, and it is not longer effective nor economic to continue the combat or fighting at that particular location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And, usually, the decision to retreat is made by a commander, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, in normal armed forces, this would be so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we should not forget that also terrorist groups also have their own leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. And these "leaders," as you call them, if we refer to the leaders of terrorist groups, since they're leaders, logically they would tell members of the group what to do, right? That's what makes them a leader?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One can assume so, under the condition that they have organised manner of carrying out their activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And logically, then, if you have leadership who tells people what to do, the members of the group are supposed to carry out the wishes of the leader, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we discussing a terrorist group or armed forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Terrorist group.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I have never been a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. Isn't it true, Dr. Markovski, that, in the military sense, the term "fortifications" normally refers to an activity that could be offensive or defensive to help a particular armed group?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the general sense, yes. But, here, we are discussing a specific situation that I already explained. I remember it well. And that is why there is no need for special fortification because protection is provided by the forest to the north-west of Slupcane, and they used this opportunity to place the mortar and fire on the security forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I forget, I would seek to tender what is 65 ter 1118.11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P00602. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Earlier today, when we were talking about the classic armed conflict in country X, one of the things that we agreed upon was that, unfortunately, oftentimes, there are abuses committed by both sides against civilians. I'd like to explore that with you, and if you could turn to what is --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think what we need to do now, Your Honours, if we can, please, is distribute the remaining binders, binders 2, 3, and 4. Then, perhaps, if the third binder could be given to the witness, please, for him to review. I'm very grateful to the court officers for their assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Dr. Markovski, perhaps if you could turn to what is tab 75 in that binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If we could show what is Exhibit P00326. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Dr. Markovski, this is a photograph taken in May of 2001, and it reportedly depicts injuries received by an ethnic Albanian man when he was held at the Kumanovo police station during that month. I wanted to ask you, in your report, you talk about crimes committed by the members of the NLA, and I wanted to ask you whether you've also been aware of crimes that were committed by members of the security forces during the crisis time in 2001.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Never heard of such a thing?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never found any such document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, apart from finding a document, did you ever hear such allegations on the news?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please remind me and then we could comment, because I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During 2001, did you ever see any news reports alleging that members of the Macedonian security forces had committed crimes or abuses against ethnic Albanian civilians.

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. But let's discuss specific problems, then we could comment. I might have read, I might have seen something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I guess my question is: Going back to what we talked about earlier, if both sides in the events of 2001 committed some crimes against civilians, that would, unfortunately, be another -- that would be one of the characteristics of the classic armed conflict that we talked about, right?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look here, the state organs such as the security structures in the Republic of Macedonia act pursuant to laws. Pursuant to that same law, they are disciplinary and criminally libel if they overstep their powers. The terrorist organisations do not adhere to any laws, and I don't see a possibility to have a parallel or comparison between the one and the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's interesting, but that's not what I asked you. I need you to answer the question that I ask you. Going back to what we talked about earlier, if both sides in the events of 2001 committed some crimes against civilians, that would, unfortunately, be one of the characteristics found in a classic armed conflict, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: BLAGOJA MARKOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are speaking again about some sides to the conflict. What I'm telling you is that if this the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia would commit something contrary to the law, they would be liable. I have not read anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
